page: Microsoft Azure FX48-24ms_v2 is a memory-intensive virtual machine powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at a high clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The configuration provides 24 vCPUs across 12 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with a massive 1008.0 GB of RAM, yielding an exceptionally high memory allocation of 42.0 GB per core. The processor includes a substantial 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions for accelerated matrix operations.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates top-tier single-core performance, highlighted by a Geekbench single-core score of 2356.0 and a top-tier text processing score of 2987.0. Multi-core performance is also strong, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 16629.0. Memory performance is robust, showing a strong write bandwidth of 120.35 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. Single-threaded tasks benefit from the high clock speed, as evidenced by strong results in gzip compression at 34.54 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 14.33 GB/sec. For lightweight AI workloads, it achieves a top-tier text generation speed of 336.04 tokens/sec using a small 135M LLM model.

This server does not include local storage or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, meaning storage requirements must rely on external Premium Storage options. The absence of a dedicated GPU limits its utility for heavy parallel training workloads, though its AMX support aids CPU-based inference. Given the massive memory-to-vCPU ratio and high clock speed, this instance is highly cost-efficient for memory-bound workloads that require rapid single-core execution without needing a high vCPU count. It is ideally suited for large in-memory databases, heavy text processing pipelines, enterprise resource planning systems, and memory-intensive data analytics.
